judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the third body paragraph of an English article shown in The Conversation's Brazil edition. The snapshot shows the html element with lang="pt-BR". The article and its articleBody container have no lang attribute, and the only other lang on the page is on the hidden consent host. The raw HTML I fetched live on 2026-10-24 is the same. So this English passage is identified as pt-BR, which fails the H58 test and 3.1.2. One could argue the page's default language is English, since the article is most of the text, and call this a 3.1.1 failure instead. Either way, this passage's language is identified wrongly, so the finding stands.

judgments.label: true_positive

A screen reader would read it with Portuguese rules, so its language is not correctly identified: a 3.1.2 failure as reported. A 3.1.1 framing, with English as the page default, is also possible, but the passage is identified wrongly either way.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the Creative Commons logo in the republish panel. Both the crop and the SVG source show the "cc creative commons" wordmark, with no BY or ND icons. The alt "CC BY ND" names Creative Commons and the article's actual licence, CC BY-ND. It is true that the image does not show "BY ND", but 1.1.1 asks for a text alternative that serves the same purpose, not a literal description. Here the purpose is to show the content is under a Creative Commons licence, which the alt conveys accurately, and the text next to it says "licença Creative Commons". The extra licence detail is true and misleads no one, so this is not a 1.1.1 failure.
